questions.prompt: Why should queries be processed in increasing value order?

choices.label: So intervals can be added once their starts are reached.
choices.feedback: An advancing query value allows a single forward pass through intervals sorted by start.

choices.label: So answers can always be returned in sorted query order.
choices.feedback: An advancing query value allows a single forward pass through intervals sorted by start.

choices.label: So the interval ends never need to be checked.
choices.feedback: An advancing query value allows a single forward pass through intervals sorted by start.

questions.prompt: Which interval should be read from the heap for a query?

choices.label: The first interval ever added, regardless of its end.
choices.feedback: The heap prioritizes interval length, but an expired front candidate must be removed before choosing an answer.

choices.label: The interval with the latest ending point.
choices.feedback: The heap prioritizes interval length, but an expired front candidate must be removed before choosing an answer.

choices.label: The shortest candidate after removing heap-front intervals whose ends are before the query.
choices.feedback: The heap prioritizes interval length, but an expired front candidate must be removed before choosing an answer.
